chapterTag.category: AP Calc AB Unit 4 — Contextual Applications

body.en: Unit 4 · Contextual Applications of Differentiation covers essential College Board AP Calculus AB competencies across foundational mechanics, intermediate analysis, and advanced FRQ problem solving.

blocks.heading: Level 1 · Foundations — Rates of Change in Context & Linear Motion

body.en: Relate position s(t), velocity v(t) = s'(t), acceleration a(t) = v'(t), and speed |v(t)|. Speed increases when v and a share the same sign.
Velocity \(v(t) = s'(t)\). Acceleration \(a(t) = v'(t)\). Speed \(= |v(t)|\). A particle speeds up when \(v(t)\) and \(a(t)\) have the same sign; slows down when opposite signs.

question.en:
Level 1 · Foundations

A particle moves with position \(s(t) = t^3 - 6t^2 + 9t\). At what values of \(t\) is the particle at rest?

solution.en: The particle is at rest when \(v(t) = s'(t) = 0\): \[ v(t) = 3t^2 - 12t + 9 = 3(t^2 - 4t + 3) = 3(t - 1)(t - 3) = 0. \] The particle is at rest at \(t = 1\) and \(t = 3\).

blocks.heading: Level 2 · Medium — Related Rates of Change

body.en: Set up geometric relationships, differentiate with respect to time t, and substitute instantaneous values.

question.en:
Level 2 · Medium

The radius \(r\) of a circle is expanding at a rate of 3 cm/s. At what rate is the area of the circle increasing when \(r = 10\text{ cm}\)?

solution.en: Area formula: \(A = \pi r^2\). Differentiate with respect to time \(t\): \[ \frac{dA}{dt} = 2\pi r \frac{dr}{dt}. \] Substitute \(r = 10\) and \(\frac{dr}{dt} = 3\): \[ \frac{dA}{dt} = 2\pi(10)(3) = \mathbf{60\pi\text{ cm}^2/\text{s}} \approx 188.50\text{ cm}^2/\text{s}. \]

blocks.heading: Level 3 · Advanced — Linear Approximations & L'Hospital's Rule for Indeterminate Limits

body.en: Construct tangent line linearizations \(L(x) = f(a) + f'(a)(x - a)\) and apply L'Hospital's Rule for 0/0 and inf/inf forms.

question.en:
Level 3 · Advanced

Evaluate the limit using L'Hospital's Rule: \(\lim_{x\to 0} \frac{e^{3x} - 1 - 3x}{x^2}\).

solution.en: Direct substitution yields \(0/0\). Apply L'Hospital's Rule: \[ \lim_{x\to 0} \frac{3e^{3x} - 3}{2x} \quad (\text{still } 0/0). \] Apply L'Hospital's Rule a second time: \[ \lim_{x\to 0} \frac{9e^{3x}}{2} = \frac{9e^0}{2} = \mathbf{\frac{9}{2}} = 4.5. \]
